topic: Anatomy of Dicot and Monocot Roots
title: What Is Inside a Root? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A garden cable, a sunflower root and a maize root: cut them across and all three show layers. Aarav pulls a weed by the bicycle track and asks how a root thinner than a pencil holds so much inside.

You will read a root section from outside in: epiblema with root hairs, cortex, the endodermis with its casparian strips (with water forced through the cells), the pericycle where side roots begin, and the stele. Then the xylem of a root being laid out: radial bundles, protoxylem at the outer edge and exarch xylem, a cambium ring in the dicot root and none in the monocot root. Then dicot vs monocot roots side by side, a pause and think check, a worked sorting example, the exam trap about the pericycle, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to answer. This is Episode 52 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
